ai.description: This 25–30 mm frog is brown with dark mottling. Males display a distinctive foot-flagging behavior, extending and waving their hind limbs to signal. It inhabits fast-flowing streams in the Western Ghats.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus fuscus* is best distinguished by its distinct, uniform reddish-brown to dark brown dorsum lacking the prominent light-colored mid-dorsal stripe seen in many congeners.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus fuscus* inhabits rocky, fast-flowing streams within evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kalakkad dancing frog performs rhythmic "foot-flagging" displays, extending and waving its hind legs to attract mates and signal rivals amidst the noise of rushing streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus fuscus* is an oviparous species that breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs in hidden crevices within forest stream beds.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus fuscus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in India, primarily inhabiting the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kalakkad Dancing Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic series of chirps near fast-flowing, rocky forest streams, where males also perform foot-flagging to attract mates.
